primary_crossing.method: Exact binomial intervals, Bonferroni over four specified cells; derive the two larger-minus-smaller difference intervals. Success is a negative interval at .05 and positive interval at .06.
primary_crossing.interpretation: Prespecified simultaneous opposite-sign anchor contrast; neither proves a unique common crossing nor an asymptotic threshold.

secondary_crossing.method: equal-tail exact Clopper-Pearson; Bonferroni over all 28 binomial cells
secondary_crossing.secondary_note: All size-pair/adjacent compatibility regions were prespecified as secondary diagnostics; the primary check uses four anchor cells.
secondary_crossing.interpretation: Zero-compatible regions are conditional on piecewise-linear interpolation of probability bounds. Adjacent-pair compatibility does not guarantee a common ordinate for all sizes. The all-pair secondary intersection is equivalent to max_L lower_L(p)<=min_L upper_L(p), hence all-size common-crossing compatibility. Neither establishes existence, uniqueness, or an asymptotic threshold; edge-touching regions are truncated by the sampled grid.

independent_size_model.model: independent unconstrained quadratic-logit curve for each size

goodness_of_fit.interpretation: Plug-in parametric bootstrap calibration, not an exact finite-sample test. Plus-one tail probability uses numerically successful fits; exact 95% binomial interval describes Monte Carlo tail-frequency uncertainty, not physical parameter uncertainty. Failure bounds assign all failed refits to either tail outcome.

Plus-one tail probability uses numerically successful fits; exact 95% binomial interval describes Monte Carlo tail-frequency uncertainty, not physical parameter uncertainty. old_raw_crossing_rule.calibration: Rejection rate of the original raw-sign guard under the fitted common-scaling null, refitting pc in every replicate; not a new circuit experiment.

bootstrap.interval_population: all converged finite common refits, including boundary/nonmonotone flags
